acceptance_criteria: The taxonomy is written into the HTGR scoping docs, and every HTGR V&V write-up carries its tier tag.
description:
Adopt and document a four-tier taxonomy for validation-data provenance, and tag every HTGR V&V claim with its tier. The failure this prevents: a Tier 3 comparison getting written up as if it were Tier 1.

  Tier 1  Open specification WITH tabulated experimental data
          e.g. IAEA-TECDOC-1382, TECDOC-1694, IRPhEP HTR10-GCR-RESR-001
  Tier 2  Open code-to-code benchmark, NO experimental data
          e.g. OECD MHTGR-350 -- VERIFICATION only, never validation
  Tier 3  Digitised from published figures
          e.g. HTTR LOFC plots in JNST 51(11-12) 2014
  Tier 4  GATED -- requires NEA framework membership
          e.g. OECD/NEA LOFC joint project, HTGR T/H (HTTF) benchmark

TIER 4 IS OUT OF SCOPE: Singapore is not an NEA member. Tier 4 requires a partner institution holding the agreement. Treat as out of scope until a collaboration exists.

This complements, and does not replace, the existing kovan open/proprietary split (which is about REDISTRIBUTION rights); the tier is about EVIDENTIAL strength.
title: HTGR cross-cutting: validation-data ACCESS TIER taxonomy, tagged on every V&V claim

description:
Found 2026-08-12 while cross-checking the new six-equation solver against the four-equation one (op-62vf). Pinned by two_fluid_tests::the_two_solvers_disagree_in_the_single_phase_limit_and_the_compliance_ratio_explains_it.

THE FINDING. Run both 1-D solvers on the SAME single-phase subcooled state (7 MPa, 500 K, 1 m x 0.05 m pipe, 8 cells, closed left, 0.05 m/s prescribed outflow, dt = 100 us, 100 steps), with the drift-flux drift velocity set to zero and the two-fluid drag set to 1e12 so the no-slip limit is exact (measured slip 2.428613e-17 m/s). They should reduce to the same equations. They do not:

  drift-flux pressure drop = 4.273288e5 Pa
  two-fluid  pressure drop = 7.813506e5 Pa
  ratio                    = 1.828453
  worst discrepancy        = 45.4 % of the pressure change

THE CAUSE, MEASURED. The two pressure equations linearise different derivatives:
  - drift_flux uses psi_h = d(rho_m)/dp at FIXED ENTHALPY, on the argument that a segregated solve freezes h while it corrects p.
  - two_fluid uses d(rho_k)/dp along the ISENTROPIC path dh_k = dp/rho_k, on the argument that the energy equation applies the reversible work term alpha_k dp/dt in the SAME step, so that is the path the state actually takes.

Measured at 7 MPa / 500 K: psi_h = 9.764946e-7, psi_s = 6.313400e-7 s^2/m^2, ratio 1.546702. A smaller compliance gives a larger pressure change, so the direction is predicted and 82 % of the magnitude is accounted for.

WHAT IS UNRESOLVED, AND MUST NOT BE ASSERTED EITHER WAY:
1. WHICH ONE IS RIGHT. The isentropic derivative is the one an acoustic response should carry, and BOTH solvers apply the work term in their energy equations, which is an argument that drift_flux is the inconsistent one. That is an argument, not a result. Nothing has been compared against an analytic water-hammer solution, a speed-of-sound measurement, or an experiment.
2. THE REMAINING 18 %. The compliance ratio 1.547 does not fully account for the observed 1.828. Two unchecked candidates: the compliances are evaluated once at the initial state whereas both solvers re-evaluate theirs as p falls (drift flux switching to a secant after its first corrector), and the two reach their end state through different numbers of outer correctors. Instrument the per-step compliance of both rather than reasoning about it.

DO NOT 'FIX' drift_flux ON THE STRENGTH OF THIS. Its gated Edwards-O'Brien benchmark (edwards_drift_flux_gs1_pressure_history: RMSE 29.0 psia, plateau 354.3 psia inside the experimental band) was measured with psi_h. Changing its compliance changes that result and would invalidate the recorded numbers. The correct order is: settle 1 above against a reference first, then change one solver, then re-measure Edwards.

SUGGESTED NEXT STEP: a closed-form check. A rigid closed pipe of subcooled water with a small prescribed outflow has an analytic acoustic response p(t) set by 1/(rho c^2). Compare both solvers against IF97's own speed of sound (tampines_steam_tables w_tp / w_tpx_eqm) rather than against each other.
title: tampines: drift-flux and two-fluid pressure equations linearise DIFFERENT compressibilities -- measured 45% disagreement in the single-phase limit, undecided which is right

description:
GOAL: 'cargo check -p <crate> --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown' passes for all 36 workspace members, and stays passing.

MEASURED BASELINE 2026-09-04 (wasm32-unknown-unknown target installed, --lib, default features): 20 PASS / 16 FAIL.

PASS (20): chem-eng-real-time-process-control-simulator, kovan-codegen, kovan-common, kovan-literature, outram-foam-appbuilder-lib, outram-foam-basic-lib, outram-foam-cli, outram-foam-mesh, outram-foam-multiphase, outram-foam-turbulence-lib, outram-park-fork-cfmesh, outram-park-fork-coolprop, outram-park-fork-dwsim-libs, outram-park-fork-liggghts, outram-park-fork-moltres, outram-park-fork-offbeat, outram-park-fork-onix, outram-park-fork-thermochimica, tampines-steam-tables, teh-o-prke.

FAIL (16), in six distinct classes — one child bead per class:
  A. rayon/rayon-core does not build on wasm ('cannot find module or crate sys'): boon-lay, nee_soon, njoy-outram-park-fork, outram-mc-libs, raffles
  B. faer default features pull rayon -> spindle -> atomic-wait ('cannot find module or crate platform'): bedok, outram-blender
  C. getrandom/uuid need an explicit wasm randomness backend: kovan, outram-park-digital-twin-engine, tampines, tuas_boussinesq_solver
  D. std::os::unix used directly: kovan-discovery, kovan-metrics, kovan-semantics
  E. 64-bit usize assumptions (E0080 shift overflow — wasm32 usize is 32-bit): outram-park-fork-pflotran, outram-park-mpi
  F. keep it from regressing (CI gate)

*** CRITICAL SCOPE CAVEAT — COMPILES IS NOT RUNS. ***
This epic's acceptance is COMPILATION only, and that must not be overstated. std::thread::spawn, std::fs and Instant::now all COMPILE for wasm32 and fail only at RUNTIME (spawn and Instant panic; fs errors). chem-eng-real-time-process-control-simulator is the proof: it PASSES the compile check today while containing 5 thread::spawn sites and 10 files using std::fs.

Non-exhaustive runtime-hostility census (src/ only, excluding tests), for the crates that will actually need to RUN in a browser:
  tuas_boussinesq_solver         spawn=27 instant=21 fs=2
  outram-park-digital-twin-engine spawn=7  instant=13 fs=2
  chem-eng-...-control-simulator spawn=5  instant=2  fs=10
  kovan                          spawn=2  instant=6  fs=36
  njoy-outram-park-fork          spawn=0  instant=1  fs=16

Making a crate RUN on wasm is per-crate work tracked separately — see epic op-eeqw (htgr_sim_v1 browser demo, GH #39), whose Phase 2 and Phase 3 are exactly that job for the htgr dependency chain. Do not close this epic claiming browser-readiness.

Established in-workspace precedent to copy rather than reinvent: outram-foam-basic-lib already passes because its rayon sits behind an off-by-default 'parallel' feature (bead op-yvj.4.1 / GH #10). That is the shape class A should adopt.

Also note this is a NEW target, not a replacement: nothing here may break the existing aarch64-linux-android gates (epic op-zfr).

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
Done, with the scope the maintainer set on 2026-09-04.

RESULT: scripts/check-wasm.sh reports 30 ok, 0 failed, 6 excluded. Every in-scope workspace member's library compiles for wasm32-unknown-unknown, and a gate plus a CLAUDE.md section keep it that way. Baseline at the start of the epic was 20/36.

Checking SCOPE rather than child count, per the lesson from op-6w0: 4 of 6 children delivered, 2 cancelled as out of scope by maintainer decision (bedok/outram-blender on faer; the four filesystem-bound kovan crates). The remaining scope IS complete for the crates that are in it.

What the classes turned into:
  A rayon        DONE — 5 crates. Target-gated off wasm ONLY, never feature-gated and never off Android, because rayon is pure Rust and Android-in-scope. Serial wasm_par shims where needed; numerically exact for these crates.
  B faer         CANCELLED — bedok/outram-blender excluded.
  C getrandom    DONE — two different getrandom majors needing two different mechanisms; one satisfied via .cargo/config.toml, one CUT by gating async-opcua off wasm.
  D std::os::unix CANCELLED — kovan crates excluded; kovan-codegen/-common/-literature kept in the gate since they already pass.
  E 32-bit usize DONE — a real latent bug, see below.
  F gate + docs  DONE.

THE MOST VALUABLE THING THIS EPIC FOUND was not a wasm issue at all. outram-park-mpi's 'COLL_CONTEXT_OFFSET: usize = 1 << 40' is a compile-time overflow on ANY 32-bit target. Fixed by widening to u64 rather than truncating, because it is a namespace tag and not a memory size. It would equally have failed on armv7-linux-androideabi and i686-linux-android — targets CLAUDE.md claims to support but whose acceptance command names only aarch64. Filed against op-zfr; I expect more width assumptions there.

Second finding, recorded in CLAUDE.md: wgpu's WebGPU backend holds Rc<Cell<u32>> and is therefore !Send on wasm, so the 'static OnceLock<Option<GpuContext>>' pattern this workspace uses in several crates cannot compile there. It needs thread_local!, which is a real change rather than a gate. Currently sidestepped by gating GPU modules off wasm.

THE CAVEAT THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH THIS RESULT: compiling is not running. thread::spawn, Instant::now and std::fs all compile for wasm and fail at run time. chem-eng-real-time-process-control-simulator passes the gate today with 5 spawn sites and 10 std::fs files. Nobody should read '30/30' as browser-readiness — the actual runtime work is epic op-eeqw (GH #39). This is stated in the epic, in the script header and at the top of the CLAUDE.md section, deliberately in all three places.

No human V&V is claimed.

title: workspace: wasm32-unknown-unknown as a supported target for every crate
